title: Bad key buggy program
statement: How many integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le 100$ are such that $n^2 + n + 1$ is divisible by $7$?
hints: The expression's divisibility by $7$ depends only on the remainder of $n$.
Test the seven remainders, then count how often the good ones occur up to $100$.
solution: Divisibility by $7$ depends only on $n$ modulo $7$. Testing the residues shows we need $n \equiv 2$ or $4 \pmod 7$. Among $1, \dots, 98$ there are $14$ numbers in each class, giving $28$, and $99$ and $100$ both fail. The total is $28$.
check_program: print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 100) if (n*n + n + 1) % 7 == 0))
